title: Assurance of Salvation
definition: Assurance of salvation is the believer's confidence, grounded in Christ and God's promises, that they belong to God and are kept by His grace.
summary: Believers can have confidence in salvation because Christ saves, keeps, and intercedes for His people.
christFocus: Assurance rests in the finished work of Christ, the promises of God, and the witness of the Spirit rather than in perfect personal performance.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Assurance of salvation is not prideful presumption. It is confidence rooted in Christ, His finished work, God's promises, and the Spirit's witness. Believers can know that eternal life is found in the Son.

Assurance does not mean believers never struggle with doubt. Scripture gives promises, evidences of grace, and the ministry of the Spirit to strengthen faith. The focus remains on Christ, not on emotional certainty.

True assurance encourages holiness rather than carelessness. Those who know they are held by grace are moved to love, obedience, gratitude, and perseverance.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many sincere believers struggle with fear that they are not saved, especially when they see weakness or remember past failure. Assurance matters because it directs the trembling heart to Christ's keeping power rather than self-confidence.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Look to Christ and His promises when doubt rises. Examine your life honestly, but do not make your performance the foundation of assurance. Keep returning to the Gospel, prayer, Scripture, and fellowship.
